answer: Cluster keys by how they grade. Each juror's scores on co-seated rows form a vector: honest strangers agree about 70% of the time, while clones running one model and prompt mirror each other near 98%. Once two keys pass 90% agreement over 40 shared rows, they merge into one payout. A farm can inject noise, but then it drifts from the jury median and loses grading pay. Like a lagoon seeping into karst, its margin drains away: 1,000 entry fees buy roughly one share.
